Does this sound familiar?

You’re capable of more. Your goals don’t always show it.

  • You set a goal with real energy, and by March it has quietly slipped.

Here’s what you’ll learn

Five things we’ll cover in 60 minutes

Why most goals fail before they start

The research on what separates goals that get reached from goals that fade, and the one mistake almost everyone makes.

How to set a goal that’s hard enough

Why a specific, difficult goal tends to beat “just do your best”, and how to find the right level of stretch.

Authentic grit, and the kind to avoid

The difference between healthy perseverance and the stubborn kind that keeps you stuck.

Making your success visible

Simple ways to make sure your effort and results get seen by the people who matter.

Your next step

How to keep going after the class, on your own or with support.

Script 1 · “By February”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“Most goals set in January are gone by February. And it usually isn’t a willpower problem.”

Body

“I’ve spent my career studying goal science, and the pattern is clear. Goals fade when they’re vague, when they’re too easy to feel exciting, or when nobody can see the progress. Fix those three things and following through gets a lot more likely.”

CTA

“I’m teaching exactly how in a free live masterclass. Tap Sign up to save a seat.”

Shot: talking to camera, natural light, your usual setting. On-screen text: “gone by February?”

Script 2 · “Authentic grit”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“Not all grit is good grit. Here’s the difference.”

Body

“Authentic grit is choosing a hard goal you actually care about and sticking with it. The other kind is pushing on with something that stopped serving you years ago, just because quitting feels like failing. Knowing which one you’re in changes everything about how you set your next goal.”

CTA

“I go deeper on this in my free masterclass. 60 minutes, live, with a replay. Tap Sign up below.”

Shot: talking to camera, one cut to a text card: “authentic grit” and “stubborn grit” side by side.

Hook (0 to 3s)

“I wrote a whole book on the science of big goals. Here’s the part readers ask me about most.”

Body

Mistake 3: great progress that nobody sees.

Fix all three and you’ve got a big goal.
